excerpt: Here “intermediate scale” refers to the size of quantum computers which will be available in the next few years, with a number of qubits ranging from 50 to a few hundred. 50 qubits is a significant milestone, because that’s beyond what can be simulated by brute force using the most powerful existing digital supercomputers. “Noisy” emphasizes that we’ll have imperfect control over those qubits; the noise will place serious limitations on what quantum devices can achieve in the near term.
overview: This passage defines the NISQ scale and states the source's core constraint: devices large enough to strain brute-force classical simulation are still noisy enough that their computational reach is sharply limited. It grounds both the opportunity and the caution in the paper's central framing.
title: 50-Qubit Classical Barrier
